title: German
description: Everyday German: greetings, family, food, numbers, getting around and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: 'Du' is the informal 'you'. Use 'Sie' (always with a capital S) with strangers: 'Wie heißen Sie?'

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
units.tip: All German nouns start with a capital letter, and each has a gender: der (masculine), die (feminine), das (neuter).

units.title: Food and drink
units.tip: 'Kein' means 'no / not any': 'Ich trinke keine Milch' = I do not drink milk.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
units.tip: Say 'eins' when counting, but 'ein' or 'eine' before a noun: 'ein Apfel', 'eine Tasse'.

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
units.tip: 'Links' is left and 'rechts' is right. Use 'fahren' when you travel by car, train or bus, and 'gehen' when you walk.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
units.tip: Careful: 'morgen' means tomorrow, but 'der Morgen' is the morning.
